messages.subject: manipulation of lists
parts:
I'm working on a problem which is exposing my ignorance of how to manipulate lists. I have a list of lists, where the first list is a set of candidate specific lists. Within each candidate's list, the first element is a data frame consisting of biographical data, and the subsequent elements are data frames consisting of group ratings of the candidate.

An indicative example is provided below

library(plyr)

df1.l<- rlply(3, data.frame(cand = sample(letters, 1),
                            y.start = sample(1980:1990, 1),
                            y.end = sample(1991:2012, 1)))
df2.l<- rlply(9, data.frame(group = rep(c(paste(sample(letters, size=4, replace = T), sep = "")), times = 4),
                            year = sample(1990:2012, size = 4),
                            score = runif(4,0,1)))

a <- list(df1.l[[1]],df2.l[[1]], df2.l[[2]],df2.l[[3]])
b <- list(df1.l[[2]],df2.l[[4]], df2.l[[5]],df2.l[[6]])
d <- list(df1.l[[3]],df2.l[[7]], df2.l[[8]],df2.l[[9]])

biglist <- list(a,b,d)

Ideally, I want a data frame, where every candidate's biographical details are appended to their group assessments. That is, each candidate's data frames will be bound by rows, and then this frame will be column bound with the candidate's biographical details.

For instance, the element biglist[[1]] will eventually become



  cand y.start y.end  group year     score
1    m    1989  2004  g     1993 0.9033009
2    m    1989  2004  l     1995 0.7066574
3    m    1989  2004  q     2004 0.1573602


what complicates things is that the ratings data frame within each candidate element are heterogeneous in two ways--there are a changing number of these frames, and each rating frame is itself possessed of a different number of rows.


I tried to use an llply call to split biglist into candidate specific lists, and then use an ldply call within this function to bind the data frames my required way, but I got nowhere. 

Any assistance you can provide will be hugely appreciated!

>

> 1 m 1989 2004 g 1993 0.9033009

>
> 3 m 1989 2004 q 2004 0.1573602

> candidate element are heterogeneous in two ways--there are a changing
> number of these frames, and each rating frame is itself possessed of

Does this give you what you want?

llply(biglist, function(l) {cbind(l[1], do.call(rbind, l[-1]))})

I'm only using llply to iterate through the list of candidates. The
binding of dataframes (rbinding all but the first, cbinding the first to
that) is just a single function. I could replace the do.call(rbind...)
part with another plyr call

llply(biglist, function(l) {cbind(l[1], ldply(l[-1], identity))})

Both these approaches will handle the heterogeneities you describe; the
latter will also handle the columns of group assessment data.frames
being different (with NA's filling in where columns don't exist).

--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University
